title: A palace in time
hook: the fourth visit: a Friday table, two candles, and a day that stops the week
carry: shabbat: a day made holy by stopping
tomorrow: guided visits: what a Christian means by grace

segments.voice: Yesterday, dhikr: the heart coming back to God's name, and Bilal's one word. Today, a fourth house.

Friday, just before sunset. A kitchen that's been busy all afternoon goes suddenly still. The table has a white cloth, two braided loaves under a cover, a cup of wine or grape juice. Someone strikes a match and lights two candles, then draws her hands in toward her face and covers her eyes. Phones go face down, or away entirely, until Saturday night. From here to nightfall tomorrow, this house is keeping a day the Torah sets apart on its first page. Today, what a Jew means by Shabbat.

segments.voice: Shabbat comes from a Hebrew root that means to stop, to cease. It begins on the first page of the Torah. After six days of making the world, the text says, in the 1917 Jewish Publication Society translation: "And God blessed the seventh day, and hallowed it." The twentieth-century rabbi Abraham Joshua Heschel pointed out that the first thing the Bible makes holy isn't a place or a person. It's a day. Later, the Ten Commandments give Shabbat twice, with two different verbs. In Exodus: "Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy." In Deuteronomy: observe it. Jewish tradition says God spoke both words at once, and some families say that's why there are two candles. Remember is the inside of the day: rest, blessing, the meal, the singing. Observe is the outside: the work you set down. Orthodox Jews refrain from thirty-nine kinds of creative work the rabbis listed; many Jews keep the day in other ways. What they share is the stop. Heschel called Shabbat a palace built in time rather than space. And it ends with a flame, a braided candle at Saturday nightfall and a blessing called havdalah, separation. Now, from your own door. Hindus have no weekly day of rest kept by everyone. Hindu holy time follows the moon instead: ekadashi fasts twice a month, festivals, a weekday some families keep for Shiva or Hanuman. The honest difference: on Shabbat, a whole people stops together, every seventh day, because the Torah's first page made a day holy.

segments.voice: Put the phone face down or out of reach, and let your hands be still, the way they'd be once a candle is lit. Let the list of unfinished things stay unfinished; it will still be there later. Breathe in: stop; breathe out: rest, a guest keeping quiet at someone else's table while they keep their day.
Shabbat, from a root meaning to stop, the seventh day made holy.

howItsDone: Jews welcome Shabbat at sundown on Friday by lighting candles and blessing wine and bread, rest through Saturday with prayer, meals and family, and close it at nightfall with havdalah; how strictly work is set aside differs among Orthodox, Conservative, Reform and other Jews.
